prompt: Given a string, find the length of the longest stretch of consecutive characters that contains no repeated character.
why: Contiguous + longest + a rule you can update one character at a time. Grow right; shrink left when a repeat enters.
trap: Two pointers also has two indices, but here both only move forward and the range between them must stay valid.

prompt: Given an array of positive integers and a target, return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least the target.
why: All positive → extending only raises the sum, trimming only lowers it. Shrink from the left while still valid.
trap: With negatives you'd need prefix sums. “Positive” is the tell that the window is safe.

prompt: Given daily temperature readings and a number k, find the highest average over any k consecutive days.
why: Fixed-size window: add the newest day, drop the oldest, track the best sum.
trap: A heap of the k hottest readings picks days that aren't consecutive.

prompt: A binary array is given along with an integer k. You may flip at most k zeros to ones. Return the longest run of consecutive ones you can get.
why: The window is valid while it holds ≤ k zeros. Expand; shrink when it holds too many.
trap: “At most k” + “longest contiguous” is the classic variable-window signature. Don't actually flip anything.

prompt: Given two strings, decide whether any rearrangement of the shorter one appears as a contiguous substring of the longer one.
why: Fixed window of the short string's length; slide it and compare letter counts.
trap: Generating every rearrangement explodes. Compare frequency counts instead.

prompt: Given strings s and t, find the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t, including duplicates.
why: Expand until the window covers t, then shrink from the left while it still covers.
trap: Binary searching on the length works but is slower, and still needs a window check inside.

prompt: You may change up to k characters of an uppercase string. What is the longest substring you can make where every letter is the same?
why: The window is valid while (length − count of its most common letter) ≤ k.
trap: Tracking “most frequent” tempts a heap. A 26-slot count array is enough.

prompt: Walking along a row of trees, you pick fruit from consecutive trees, but each of your two baskets can hold only one type. What's the most fruit you can collect?
why: Strip the story: longest contiguous run with at most 2 distinct values.
trap: The story hides the shape. Rewrite it as “longest subarray with ≤ k distinct”.

prompt: Return the largest sum of any 7 consecutive elements in an array of a million integers.
why: Fixed-size window: add the new element, drop the old one. O(n) with no extra memory.
trap: Prefix sums also work, but they spend O(n) memory on what a running sum does for free.

prompt: Walking along a row of trees, you collect fruit but may hold at most 2 kinds at once. What's the longest contiguous stretch you can pick?
why: Longest window with at most k distinct values: grow right, shrink left while the window holds 3 kinds.
trap: Greedy restarts at each new kind lose the overlap the window keeps.

prompt: You may replace up to k characters in a string. Find the length of the longest substring of one repeated letter you can make.
why: A window is valid if its length minus its most common letter's count is ≤ k. Grow and shrink accordingly.
trap: Binary search on the length works but is slower and harder than the direct window.
